name: Can an older house handle a major remodel or room addition?

mainEntity.name: Can an older house handle a major remodel or room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: An older home can often support a kitchen remodel, bathroom remodel, addition, ADU, garage conversion, or whole-home renovation, but the right scope depends on its existing condition and local requirements. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design develops designs around the property, intended use, and household needs rather than assuming every older house should receive the same treatment. Key factors: foundation and framing condition, utility capacity, setbacks, available space, historic characteristics, and the desired change of use. Practical guidance: request an existing-condition review before committing to a layout or purchase. Ask which conditions could require engineering, permit review, or added construction work. A staged plan can make a large renovation more manageable.
acceptedAnswer.description: Often, yes—but feasibility depends on framing, foundation, utilities, lot conditions, and the proposed changes. Have the existing structure reviewed before finalizing a kitchen, addition, ADU, garage conversion, or whole-home scope.
